statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of six public anonymous paths. Authenticated repository editing, settings, checkout, enterprise administration, and destructive account flows were not covered because they require credentials and represent separate gated archetypes.

findings.summary: The public homepage ignores the system light preference and remains dark.
findings.evidence: Computed styles stayed dark under both emulated light and dark preferences: html background rgb(13,17,23), color-scheme dark. The screenshots confirm no system-driven light retint.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the system preference as the anonymous default with color-scheme and prefers-color-scheme, while preserving an explicit user override.

findings.summary: Sampled state and route changes do not expose View Transition integration.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition integration while the sampled navigation uses full document/state swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressively enhanced same-document or cross-document View Transitions to repository, search, and menu state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Transient UI uses popover semantics but not CSS anchor positioning or fallback positions.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains a popover, but full captured page HTML/CSS contained no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for menus and tooltips where browser support and existing overlay infrastructure allow.

findings.summary: The throttled homepage has very slow paint and LCP despite stable layout.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 23.2s, FCP 13.0s, CLS 0, and TBT 180ms; a separate trace measured LCP 2.16s and TBT 178ms, showing stability but poor throttled load performance.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritise the LCP resource, reduce render-blocking CSS and JavaScript, and repeat mobile Lighthouse under consistent conditions.

findings.summary: The homepage delivery chain is large and stylesheet-heavy.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 154 requests and 4,115,544 transferred bytes, including 26 stylesheets and ten parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheet candidates confirmed in the document head.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate and route-scope critical CSS, defer non-critical page styles, and shorten the parser-discovered render-blocking chain.

findings.summary: The landing page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 828 KiB unused JavaScript and 202 KiB unused CSS; HAR recorded 100 script requests transferring 1.92 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Split landing-page features and logo/catalog modules by actual viewport need, remove duplicate framework payload, and load optional 3D sections on interaction or proximity.

findings.summary: A feature selector accessible name does not include its visible label.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified a serious accessible-name mismatch: the visible button text Code is not included in aria-label Select a GitHub feature.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure the button accessible name contains the visible Code label, for example by using visible text as the name and moving supplemental context to aria-describedby.

findings.summary: Homepage images frequently omit explicit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: Document has HTML doctype and UTF-8 charset, but image evidence found all 24 img elements lacked both explicit dimensions and Lighthouse flagged two unsized logos.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height attributes or an equivalent intrinsic aspect ratio for every content image, including customer logos.

findings.summary: Share metadata is strong, but rich entities lack JSON-LD.
findings.evidence: Homepage exposes seven accurate Open Graph fields but no JSON-LD; repository detail also exposed seven Open Graph fields and no JSON-LD for its repository entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD on the homepage and SoftwareSourceCode or appropriate schema on public repository pages when maintainable.

findings.summary: Permissions-Policy is absent and the CSP allows inline styles.
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS, DENY/frame-ancestors, nosniff, and referrer policy, but Permissions-Policy is absent and CSP permits unsafe-inline styles.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship a restrictive Permissions-Policy for unused capabilities and continue reducing inline-style dependence so CSP can avoid unsafe-inline where feasible.

findings.summary: The stylesheet still relies heavily on physical left/right properties.
findings.evidence: html lang is en and 89 logical-property rules were detected, but the same live stylesheets contained 1,425 physical left/right rules and no explicit dir, creating avoidable bidi risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate reusable layout primitives to inline/block logical properties and test representative repository and form surfaces under dir=rtl.

findings.summary: Several images are oversized or lack responsive source selection.
findings.evidence: Image audit found three oversized PNGs, 13 images without srcset, three legacy-format images, and 24 without both dimension attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive srcset/sizes, replace legacy decorative PNGs, and request assets near their rendered dimensions.

findings.summary: The homepage fetches optional 3D assets and large unused bundles before user demand.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 4.12 MB including four decorative GLB fetches totalling about 827 KB, while Lighthouse found 828 KiB unused JavaScript and 202 KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer decorative GLB and feature bundles until intersection or interaction, and avoid fetching assets for unopened sections.

findings.summary: A 4.12 MB, 154-request landing page is disproportionate to its initial task.
findings.evidence: The homepage made 154 requests and transferred 4.12 MB, including 1.92 MB scripts, a 220 KB font, 583 KB images, and 826 KB XHR/3D assets for a marketing entry page.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level transfer/request budget, lazy-load below-fold media, subset fonts, and treat decorative 3D content as optional enhancement.

findings.summary: GitHub promotes MCP but its sampled web UI does not expose browser-native structured tools.
findings.evidence: The raw page is highly machine-readable and links to an MCP Registry, but captured DOM and scripts exposed no WebMCP or browser-registered agent tools for search, repository, or sign-in capabilities.
findings.suggestedFix: Pilot narrowly scoped, confirmation-gated WebMCP tools for public repository search and read-only repository metadata instead of requiring UI scraping.

findings.summary: The anonymous marketing homepage has a large initial heap and DOM-related footprint.
findings.evidence: A single homepage state retained 1,003,253 heap nodes, 3,534,921 edges, and 62.1 MB self size, disproportionate for a public marketing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initially hydrated component and script scope, defer below-fold interactive sections, and set a heap/node budget for the landing route.
